```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Root locator + dual-load idiom shared with the bench/scenarios drivers:
# the source tree (check and site-build contexts) loads through pkgload; a
# bare installed package (reader-side) loads through library().
.pkg_root <- function() {
  for (dd in c(".", "..", "../..")) {
    if (file.exists(file.path(dd, "DESCRIPTION")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(dd, "R", "treatment-report.R"))) return(normalizePath(dd))
  }
  NA_character_
}
PKG <- .pkg_root()
if (!is.na(PKG) && requireNamespace("pkgload", quietly = TRUE)) {
  suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(pkgload::load_all(PKG, quiet = TRUE,
                                                      export_all = TRUE)))
} else {
  library(msuiter)
}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Tiny reporter for the error-message quality section: catches the
# msuiter_error_* condition and shows its class plus the full message.
show_error <- function(expr) {
  r <- tryCatch({ force(expr); "no condition raised" },
    error = function(e) {
      paste0("condition class: ", class(e)[1], "\n", conditionMessage(e))
    })
  cat(r, "\n")
}
```

## The working grammar

msuiter moves typed objects between the layers: `ms_variants()` reads and
validates caller output into an **MsVariants** input IR, `ms_tally()` runs it
through the Rust kernel into an **MsCatalog** count IR, signature work
produces an **MsSignature**, and reference knowledge arrives as an
**MsRefDb**. Every face takes and returns an inspected object, so a broken
record is caught at the boundary that owns it, with a message that names the
field, the expectation and the fix. This tour runs the whole chain end to
end on a synthetic fixture genome so the printed output below is the real
kernel output, reproducible from this page alone.

## A fixture genome in two dozen lines

The tally layer reads the reference from a UCSC twoBit file. The block
below is the same little-endian writer the test-suite helpers use, so the
trivial genome (`chr1` = `ACAC…`, `chr2` = `GCGC…`) and the variants above it
agree base for base: a C>A SNV at `chr1:12` sits in the trinucleotide
context `A[C>A]A`, one of the 96 SBS channels.

```{r fixture}
.u32le <- function(v) writeBin(as.integer(v), raw(), size = 4L, endian = "little")
.pack_bases <- function(bases) {
  out <- raw((length(bases) + 3L) %/% 4L)
  acc <- 0L; filled <- 0L; k <- 0L
  for (b in bases) {
    acc <- bitwOr(bitwShiftL(acc, 2L), b); filled <- filled + 1L
    if (filled == 4L) { k <- k + 1L; out[k] <- as.raw(acc); acc <- 0L; filled <- 0L }
  }
  if (filled > 0L) out[k + 1L] <- as.raw(bitwShiftL(acc, 2L * (4L - filled)))
  out
}
.write_2bit <- function(path) {
  chr1 <- rep(c(2L, 1L), 32L); chr1[51L:53L] <- 0L
  chr2 <- rep(c(3L, 1L), 20L)
  recs <- list(
    list(name = "chr1", size = 64L, dna = .pack_bases(chr1), nb = 50L, nl = 3L),
    list(name = "chr2", size = 40L, dna = .pack_bases(chr2),
         nb = integer(0), nl = integer(0)))
  off <- 16L + sum(vapply(recs, function(r) 1L + nchar(r$name) + 4L, 0L))
  index <- raw(); body <- raw()
  for (r in recs) {
    index <- c(index, as.raw(nchar(r$name)), charToRaw(r$name), .u32le(off))
    rec <- c(.u32le(r$size), .u32le(length(r$nb)), .u32le(r$nb), .u32le(r$nl),
             .u32le(0L), .u32le(0L), r$dna)
    body <- c(body, rec); off <- off + length(rec)
  }
  bytes <- c(.u32le(0x1A412743L), .u32le(0L), .u32le(length(recs)),
             .u32le(0L), index, body)
  con <- file(path, "wb"); on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
  writeBin(bytes, con); invisible(path)
}
genome <- file.path(tempdir(), "tour-2bit.2bit")
.write_2bit(genome)
```

## Step 1 — ms_variants(): the typed input IR

File input takes VCF/TSV/MAF (optionally gzipped); the canonical
`data.frame(chrom, start, end, ref, alt)` form is validated directly. The
parser is deliberately strict about what it will not guess: unusable alleles
are not dropped silently — they enter the provenance **skip ledger**, which
is the filter face of the io layer (the count of records that left the
stream, keyed by reason).

```{r variants}
vcf <- c(
  "##fileformat=VCFv4.2",
  "#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO",
  "chr7\t55191822\t.\tC\tT\t.\tPASS\t.",
  "chr17\t7676594\t.\tCA\tC\t.\t.\t.",
  "chr1\t100\t.\tG\t<NON_REF>\t.\tPASS\t.",
  "chr2\t200\t.\tA\t.\t.\tPASS\t.")
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".vcf"); writeLines(vcf, path)
v <- ms_variants(path, "GRCh38", caller = "synthetic", matched_normal = "none")
v
str(v@provenance$parse)
```

Two of the four data lines become records; the symbolic and missing alleles
left the stream as ledger entries `symbolic_alt` and `missing_alt`, so the
drop is auditable rather than silent.

## Step 2 — ms_tally(): the count IR through the Rust kernel

Three SNVs in two samples, tabulated over the fixture genome. The result is
an `MsCatalog`: a channels x samples count table plus the channel-registry
snapshot (name, labels and a content hash) that later objects pin against.

```{r tally}
tab <- data.frame(
  chrom  = c("chr1", "chr1", "chr1"),
  start  = c(12L, 22L, 14L),
  end    = c(12L, 22L, 14L),
  ref    = c("C", "C", "C"),
  alt    = c("A", "T", "T"),
  sample = c("S1", "S1", "S2"))
v2 <- ms_variants(tab, "GRCh38", caller = "synthetic", matched_normal = "none")
cat1 <- ms_tally(v2, genome)
cat1
```

The count table coerces on demand (`as.data.frame(cat1@counts)` gives the
plain data.frame view) and filters by the usual row selection — here the
nonzero channel queue:

```{r counts}
nz <- cat1@counts[rowSums(as.matrix(cat1@counts)) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
nz
class(as.data.frame(cat1@counts))
```

## Step 3 — ms_signature(): signatures pinned to a channel table

An `MsSignature` carries a catalog summary whose `channel_hash` is **derived
from a validated MsCatalog, never hand-forged** — the validator recomputes it
and refuses any other value, which is what stops a signature dictionary from
drifting off the channel table it was tallied against.

```{r signature}
labels <- cat1@channels$labels
sigs <- matrix((seq_len(length(labels) * 2L) * 7L + 1L) %% 10L / 10,
               length(labels), 2L,
               dimnames = list(labels, c("SIG1", "SIG2")))
exp1 <- matrix(c(40, 5, 10, 30), 2L, 2L,
               dimnames = list(c("SIG1", "SIG2"), c("S1", "S2")))
summary1 <- list(
  n_channels   = length(labels), n_samples = 2L,
  channel_name = cat1@channels$name, channel_hash = cat1@channels$hash,
  build = "GRCh38")
sig <- ms_signature(sigs, exp1, summary1, engine = "synthetic", seed = 1L)
sig
```

## Step 4 — ms_refdb(): the reference face, bundled-first

Reference dictionaries are versioned, digest-pinned objects. The bundled
COSMIC v3.6 face ships inside the package, so the trusted default needs no
download; `ms_refdb()` builds the same class from your own matrices plus the
governance metadata.

```{r refdb-bundled}
br <- ms_refdb_bundled()
names(br)
db <- br[["SBS_GRCh38"]]
db
head(db@matrices[[1]][, 1:4], 3)
```

```{r refdb-own}
ms_refdb(list(sbs = sigs), metadata = list(
  version = "1", class = "SBS", build = "GRCh38", schema_version = "1",
  sha256 = paste0(rep("a", 64), collapse = ""), license = "CC0-1.0",
  build_independent = FALSE, availability = "GRCh38"))
```

## Errors speak for themselves

Every boundary abort raises an `msuiter_error_*` condition carrying the class,
the offending value and a concrete repair step. A few live samples, run on
purpose-wrong input:

```{r errors}
forged <- summary1
forged$channel_hash <- paste0(rep("0", 64), collapse = "")
show_error(ms_signature(sigs, exp1, forged, engine = "synthetic", seed = 1L))
show_error(ms_variants(data.frame(chrom = "chr1", start = -5, end = -5,
                                  ref = "C", alt = "T"),
                        "GRCh38", caller = "s", matched_normal = "none"))
bp <- tempfile(fileext = ".bcf")
con <- file(bp, "wb"); writeBin(as.raw(c(0x42, 0x43, 0x46, 0x02)), con); close(con)
show_error(ms_variants(bp, "GRCh38", caller = "s", matched_normal = "none"))
show_error(ms_refdb(list(sbs = sigs), metadata = list(
  version = "1", class = "SBS", build = "GRCh38", schema_version = "1",
  sha256 = "tooshort", license = "CC0-1.0",
  build_independent = FALSE, availability = "GRCh38")))
unlink(bp)
```

## Where to go next

The function-to-concept-to-pillar bridge is [docs/MSU-MAP.md](https://github.com/WangLabCSU/msuiter/blob/main/docs/MSU-MAP.md);
one-row-per-export, so any face names the concept it serves and its peer
counterpart. For extending the engine registry itself see the *Extending
msuiter* article.

```{r cleanup, include = FALSE}
unlink(path); unlink(genome)
```
